texts.full_text: us over Boeing with $12.7B deal By Michael Sasso, Bloomberg Updated: 12/15/2017 11:07:31 AM EST Delta AirLines ordered 100 ofAirbus's A321neo jetliners, a deal with a list value of $12.7 billion, in a major victory for the European planemaker over Boeing. Deliveries of the single-aisle planes will begin in early 2020 and the transaction includes options for an additional 100 aircraft, Delta said in a statement Thursday. The airline's decision dealt a setback to Boeing's efforts to sell its newest 737model, the Max 10. The A321neo is "the best narrow-body product in the sky," Delta Chief Executive Officer Ed Bastian said in a presentation to investors. Delta is turning to Airbus to overhaul its short-range fleet three years after placing an order of long-haul jetliners withthe European planemaker. In recent months, the No. 2 U.S. airline has been battling Boeing in a trade dispute involving a separate plane, Bombardier's C Series. The U.S. manufacturer persuaded the Commerce Department to slap 300 percent duties on the new Canadianjet, contending that Bombardier sold it to Delta at well below cost. The Atlanta-basedairline has been navigating through various challenges in its relationship with Boeing and other manufacturers as part of a broader strategyto diversify its fleet options. This decision not only marks a significant investment for Delta but also reflects the competitive landscape within the aerospace industry. By choosing Airbus's A321neo, Delta is positioning itself at the forefront of aircraft technology

You're fabulous The best designer there GravityDecember 26, 2007 Last night was the opening performance of my sister Christian’s new play. It took place at our local theatre and it had been long-awaited by her fans - myself included. Christian has always fascinated me with how she weaves stories into life; transforming mundane scenes from everyday existence to a canvas brimming over, bursting out in the fullness of imagination that only an artist can see. This play was no different — it explored themes such as identity and belonging amidst urban sprawl. The set design by Christian herself mirrored her intricate narrative style - complex yet cohesive; chaotic but orderly within its chaos! The stage had a city-scape backdrop with high rise buildings, traffic signals flashing in the distance. And right at center was an old oak tree that stood as both witness and participant to all of what unfolded beneath it.
